source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

pt.L: E a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim, dizendo:
pt.B: A palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim:
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me deu esta mensagem:

decisions.choice: each person answers for their own sin: the theme of the chapter
decisions.reason: The exiles believed they were being punished for their ancestors' sins and that nothing they did could change it (verse 2). The LORD answers that each person is judged by their own conduct, and that anyone who turns from sin will live (verses 21-23, 30-32). The chapter is built like a case in law: a righteous man, his wicked son, and that son's righteous son (verses 5-18).

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The formula follows the wording set in the Jeremiah table.

source.text: מַה־לָּכֶ֗ם אַתֶּם֙ מֹֽשְׁלִים֙ אֶת־הַמָּשָׁ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה עַל־אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר אָבוֹת֙ יֹ֣אכְלוּ בֹ֔סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה׃

records.literal_gloss: What [is it] to you, you who speak this proverb about [the] land of Israel, saying: Fathers eat sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are blunted?

en.L: What do you mean, you who use this proverb about the land of Israel, saying, "Fathers eat sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are blunted"?
en.B: What do you mean by repeating this proverb about the land of Israel: "The {{gender:parents|fathers}} eat sour grapes, but it is the children whose teeth are set on edge"?
en.R: Why do you keep quoting this saying about the land of Israel: "The {{gender:parents|fathers}} eat the sour grapes, but the children get the sour taste"?

pt.L: Que [querem dizer] vocês, que usam este provérbio a respeito da terra de Israel, dizendo: "Pais comem uvas verdes, e os dentes dos filhos ficam embotados"?
pt.B: O que vocês querem dizer repetindo este provérbio sobre a terra de Israel: "Os pais comem uvas verdes, mas são os filhos que ficam com os dentes ásperos"?
pt.R: Por que vocês vivem repetindo este ditado sobre a terra de Israel: "Os pais comem as uvas verdes, mas são os filhos que ficam com o gosto azedo na boca"?

decisions.choice: the fathers eat sour grapes, and the children's teeth are blunted: the children suffer for their parents' sins
decisions.reason: Unripe grapes leave the teeth feeling rough and dull. The proverb says that one generation does wrong and the next pays for it. The exiles used it to say that their punishment was unfair and that they could do nothing about it.

decisions.choice: the same proverb in Jeremiah 31:29
decisions.reason: Jeremiah quotes the same proverb and says that in days to come people will no longer use it, because each will die for their own sin (Jeremiah 31:29-30). Ezekiel says that it must stop now. In Jeremiah the first verb is "ate"; here it is "eat", a saying about what always happens.

decisions.choice: blunted: made dull, set on edge
decisions.reason: As in Jeremiah 31:29.

decisions.choice: the wording of Jeremiah 31:29 at each level
decisions.reason: The proverb keeps the published wording of Jeremiah 31:29 at each level, with "eat" for "ate" (m2), and the same gender setting for "parents".

decisions.choice: the wording of Jeremiah 31:29 in Portuguese at each level, in the present ("comem", "ficam")
decisions.reason: The same proverb (m2) keeps the words Jeremiah 31:29 has in Portuguese at each level ("embotados" L, "os dentes ásperos" B, "o gosto azedo na boca" R), with the present tense, as the English says "eat" here. "Os pais" already means fathers and mothers, so Balanced and Readable need no gender setting, as in Jeremiah.

source.text: חַי־אָ֕נִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה אִם־יִֽהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם ע֗וֹד מְשֹׁ֛ל הַמָּשָׁ֥ל הַזֶּ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: [As] I live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, surely there will not be to you again [occasion] to use this proverb in Israel.

en.L: [As] I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, you will no longer have [occasion] to use this proverb in Israel.
en.B: As surely as I live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, this proverb will no longer be quoted in Israel.
en.R: As surely as I live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, you will not use this saying in Israel anymore.

pt.L: [Tão certo como] eu vivo, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, vocês não terão mais [ocasião] de usar este provérbio em Israel.
pt.B: Tão certo como eu vivo, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, este provérbio não será mais citado em Israel.
pt.R: Tão certo como eu vivo, diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, vocês não vão mais usar esse ditado em Israel.

decisions.choice: As I live, declares the Lord GOD (L); As surely as I live (B, R)
decisions.reason: The oath follows the wording set at 16:48.

source.text: הֵ֤ן כָּל־הַנְּפָשׁוֹת֙ לִ֣י הֵ֔נָּה כְּנֶ֧פֶשׁ הָאָ֛ב וּכְנֶ֥פֶשׁ הַבֵּ֖ן לִי־הֵ֑נָּה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֥יא תָמֽוּת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Look, all the souls [are] mine; as the soul of the father, so the soul of the son, [they are] mine. The soul who sins, it will die.

en.L: Look, all the souls [are] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}; as the soul of the father, so the soul of the son [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}. The soul who sins, it will die.
en.B: Every life belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the life of the {{gender:parent|father}} as well as the life of the {{gender:child|son}}; both belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. The person who sins is the one who will die.
en.R: Every person belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{gender:parents|fathers}} and {{gender:children|sons}} alike. The person who sins is the one who will die.

pt.L: Eis que todas as almas [são] {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}}; a alma do pai, tal como a alma do filho, [é] {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}}. A alma que peca, ela é que morrerá.
pt.B: Toda vida pertence a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, tanto a vida dos pais como a dos filhos; as duas pertencem a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Quem morrerá é a pessoa que pecar.
pt.R: Todas as pessoas pertencem a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, tanto os pais como os filhos. Quem vai morrer é a pessoa que pecar.

decisions.choice: the soul: the living person, a whole human life
alternatives: the soul as the part of a person that lives on after death
decisions.reason: The word *nefesh* means a living being, a person, or a life. Here it does not mean a soul as distinct from the body, but the person as a whole: every human life belongs to God. "The soul who sins" means the person who sins.

decisions.choice: the person who sins will die: each is judged for their own sin
decisions.reason: This is the answer to the proverb of verse 2. The Law already said that parents are not put to death for their children's sins nor children for their parents' (Deuteronomy 24:16). "Die" and "live" here are about the LORD's judgment: whether a person is condemned or spared and keeps their place among his people (verses 9, 13, 21). The chapter does not deny that sin harms the next generation (compare Exodus 20:5); it denies that anyone is condemned for sins they did not commit.

decisions.choice: the soul (L); the person (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *nefesh* in this verse and verse 20. Literal keeps the traditional "soul"; Balanced and Readable say "person", which is what the word means here (m1).

decisions.choice: parent, child (with father, son as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: Here the father and son stand for every parent and child, so Balanced and Readable use the gender setting, as Jeremiah 31:29 does. In the case of verses 5-18 the Hebrew describes a man, his son and his grandson, and there the words stay as they are.

decisions.choice: A alma que peca, ela é que morrerá (L); Quem morrerá é a pessoa que pecar (B); Quem vai morrer é a pessoa que pecar (R)
alternatives: A alma que pecar, essa morrerá
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "alma", Balanced and Readable say "pessoa", as the English (r-en-1). The sentence is worded afresh, putting the weight where the Hebrew puts it, on the one who sins, rather than following the familiar older wording. Verse 20 repeats it in the same words.

decisions.choice: os pais ... os filhos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a setting for "parent/father" and "child/son". Portuguese says it in the plural, "os pais", "os filhos", which already take in mothers and daughters, as Jeremiah 31:29 does, so no setting is needed; Literal keeps the singular "pai", "filho" of the Hebrew.

source.text: וְאִ֖ישׁ כִּי־יִהְיֶ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And a man, if he is righteous and does justice and righteousness,

en.L: And if a man is righteous and does justice and righteousness,
en.B: Suppose there is a man who is righteous and does what is just and right,
en.R: Suppose there is a man who is righteous. He does what is fair and right.

pt.L: E, se um homem for justo e praticar o direito e a justiça,
pt.B: Imaginem um homem que é justo e faz o que é justo e certo,
pt.R: Imaginem um homem que é justo. Ele faz o que é correto e certo.

decisions.choice: if a man is righteous: the first of three cases, set out like the cases in the Law
decisions.reason: The chapter tells of three generations: a righteous man (verses 5-9), his violent son (verses 10-13), and that son's son, who does not follow his father's ways (verses 14-18). The form is that of the Law's case laws ("if a man ...", Exodus 21; Leviticus 20). The cases are about men because some of the laws named (verses 6, 11, 15) concern a man and his neighbor's wife; the principle applies to every person (verses 4, 20).

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness: what is fair and right
decisions.reason: The pair describes a life lived by God's standards toward God and toward others (Genesis 18:19; Amos 5:24). Verses 6-9 list what it means.

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness (L); what is just and right (B); what is fair and right (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two nouns. Balanced and Readable use the adjectives, which read more naturally after "does".

decisions.choice: o direito e a justiça (L); o que é justo e certo (B); o que é correto e certo (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two nouns of the pair (m2), "direito" for mishpat, what is fair, and "justiça"; Balanced and Readable use adjectives, as the English does (r-en-1). God speaks to the exiles with "vocês" ("Imaginem").

source.text: אֶל־הֶֽהָרִים֙ לֹ֣א אָכָ֔ל וְעֵינָיו֙ לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֔א אֶל־גִּלּוּלֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאֶת־אֵ֤שֶׁת רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ לֹ֣א טִמֵּ֔א וְאֶל־אִשָּׁ֥ה נִדָּ֖ה לֹ֥א יִקְרָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: on the mountains he has not eaten, and his eyes he has not lifted to the idols of the house of Israel, and his neighbor's wife he has not defiled, and to a woman in impurity he has not come near,

en.L: [if] he has not eaten on the mountains, and has not lifted up his eyes to the filthy idols of the house of Israel, and has not defiled his neighbor's wife, and has not come near a woman in [her] impurity,
en.B: who does not eat at the mountain shrines or look to the idols of the house of Israel, who does not defile his neighbor's wife or have relations with a woman during her period,
en.R: He does not eat at the mountain shrines. He does not look to the idols of the people of Israel for help. He does not commit adultery with his neighbor's wife. He does not have sex with a woman during her monthly period.

pt.L: [se] não comer sobre os montes, nem levantar os seus olhos para os ídolos imundos da casa de Israel, nem contaminar a mulher do seu próximo, nem se aproximar de uma mulher na [sua] impureza,
pt.B: que não come nos santuários dos montes nem olha para os ídolos da casa de Israel, que não contamina a mulher do seu próximo nem tem relações com uma mulher durante a menstruação,
pt.R: Ele não come nos santuários dos montes. Não olha para os ídolos do povo de Israel pedindo ajuda. Não comete adultério com a mulher do seu vizinho. Não tem relações sexuais com uma mulher durante a menstruação.

decisions.choice: eaten on the mountains: eaten sacrificial meals at the hill shrines of other gods
decisions.reason: Sacrifices at the high places were followed by a meal, and to eat it was to take part in the worship (22:9; Hosea 4:13).

decisions.choice: lifted his eyes to the idols: looked to them in worship and for help
decisions.reason: To lift one's eyes to someone is to look to them for help (Psalm 121:1; 123:1). The idols are *gillulim* (see 6:4).

decisions.choice: his neighbor's wife ... a woman in her impurity: the laws of Leviticus
decisions.reason: Adultery with a neighbor's wife and relations with a woman during her monthly period were both forbidden (Leviticus 18:19-20; 20:10, 18). "Come near" is a polite way of speaking of sexual relations.

decisions.choice: filthy idols (L); idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *gillulim*.

decisions.choice: have relations with a woman during her period (B); have sex with a woman during her monthly period (R)
alternatives: come near a woman in her impurity
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's polite expression. Balanced and Readable state its meaning plainly, as the decision at 16:1 sets out for frank passages.

decisions.choice: tem relações com uma mulher durante a menstruação (B); tem relações sexuais (R)
alternatives: se aproxima de uma mulher impura
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-2): Literal keeps the Hebrew's polite "aproximar-se"; Balanced and Readable say plainly and soberly what the law forbids (m3), with the ordinary word "menstruação".

source.text: וְאִישׁ֙ לֹ֣א יוֹנֶ֔ה חֲבֹלָת֥וֹ חוֹב֙ יָשִׁ֔יב גְּזֵלָ֖ה לֹ֣א יִגְזֹ֑ל לַחְמוֹ֙ לְרָעֵ֣ב יִתֵּ֔ן וְעֵירֹ֖ם יְכַסֶּה־בָּֽגֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: and no one he oppresses, his pledge for a debt he returns, robbery he does not commit, his bread to the hungry he gives, and the naked he covers with clothing,

en.L: and has not oppressed anyone, has returned to the debtor his pledge, has committed no robbery, has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with clothing,
en.B: who does not oppress anyone but returns what a debtor gave him as a pledge, who does not rob but gives his food to the hungry and clothes the naked,
en.R: He does not take advantage of anyone. When someone gives him something to keep as a promise to pay back a loan, he returns it. He does not rob anyone. He gives food to hungry people and clothes to people who have nothing to wear.

pt.L: e não oprimir ninguém, devolver ao devedor o seu penhor, não cometer roubo, der o seu pão ao faminto e cobrir de roupa o nu,
pt.B: que não oprime ninguém, mas devolve o que o devedor lhe deu como penhor, que não rouba, mas dá o seu alimento ao faminto e veste o nu,
pt.R: Ele não se aproveita de ninguém. Quando alguém lhe dá alguma coisa como garantia de que vai pagar um empréstimo, ele a devolve. Ele não rouba ninguém. Dá comida a quem tem fome e roupa a quem não tem o que vestir.

decisions.choice: returns the debtor's pledge: the law of pledges
decisions.reason: A lender could take a pledge, such as a cloak, as security for a loan, but the Law required him to give back a cloak by nightfall, since the poor man had nothing else to sleep in (Exodus 22:25-26; Deuteronomy 24:10-13).

decisions.choice: gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked: care for the poor
decisions.reason: Isaiah 58:7 names the same deeds as the fasting the LORD wants.

source.text: בַּנֶּ֣שֶׁךְ לֹֽא־יִתֵּ֗ן וְתַרְבִּית֙ לֹ֣א יִקָּ֔ח מֵעָ֖וֶל יָשִׁ֣יב יָד֑וֹ מִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֱמֶת֙ יַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה בֵּ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ לְאִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: at interest he does not lend, and profit he does not take, from injustice he turns back his hand, justice of truth he does between man and man,

en.L: has not lent at interest or taken profit, has turned back his hand from injustice, has done true justice between one person and another,
en.B: who does not lend at interest or take profit, who keeps his hand from wrongdoing and judges fairly between one person and another,
en.R: He does not charge interest when he lends money, and he does not make a profit from it. He keeps away from doing wrong. He is fair when he settles disputes between people.

pt.L: não emprestar com juros nem tomar lucro, desviar a sua mão da injustiça, fizer justiça verdadeira entre uma pessoa e outra,
pt.B: que não empresta com juros nem tira lucro, que afasta a mão da maldade e julga com justiça entre uma pessoa e outra,
pt.R: Ele não cobra juros quando empresta dinheiro e não tira lucro disso. Fica longe de fazer o mal. É justo quando resolve as brigas entre as pessoas.

decisions.choice: interest and profit: the laws against making money from a needy neighbor
decisions.reason: The Law forbade an Israelite to charge interest on a loan to a fellow Israelite in need, whether in money or in food (Leviticus 25:35-37; Exodus 22:24). The two words may be two kinds of interest, or interest taken in advance and added at repayment.

decisions.choice: true justice between one person and another: fair judgment in disputes
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe a judge, or anyone called on to settle a quarrel (Zechariah 7:9).

source.text: בְּחֻקּוֹתַ֧י יְהַלֵּ֛ךְ וּמִשְׁפָּטַ֥י שָׁמַ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת אֱמֶ֑ת צַדִּ֥יק הוּא֙ חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: in my statutes he walks and my judgments he keeps, to do faithfulness — righteous he [is]; he will surely live, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: [if] he walks in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and keeps {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, acting faithfully, he [is] righteous; he will surely live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: and who follows {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and keeps {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings faithfully. That man is righteous; he will surely live, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He lives by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and is careful to obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules. A man like that is righteous. He will certainly live, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: andar nos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos e guardar os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} juízos, agindo com fidelidade, ele [é] justo; certamente viverá, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.B: e que segue os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos e guarda fielmente as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} ordenanças. Esse homem é justo; certamente viverá, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.
pt.R: Ele vive pelas {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} leis e tem o cuidado de obedecer às {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} regras. Um homem assim é justo. Ele com certeza vai viver, diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: he is righteous; he will surely live: the verdict on the case
decisions.reason: The words sound like the verdict of a priest or judge (compare Leviticus 18:5). To "live" is to be accepted by the LORD and to escape the judgment that is coming.

decisions.choice: statutes, judgments (L); statutes, rulings (B); laws, rules (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording in Ezekiel for *chuqqot* ("statutes" / "statutes" / "laws") and *mishpatim* ("judgments" / "rulings" / "rules"), as published in chapters 1-7.

source.text: וְהוֹלִ֥יד בֵּן־פָּרִ֖יץ שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ דָּ֑ם וְעָ֣שָׂה אָ֔ח מֵאַחַ֖ד מֵאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [if] he fathers a son, violent, a shedder of blood, and he does [to a brother] any one of these,

en.L: But [if] he fathers a son who is violent, a shedder of blood, who does any one of these [things],
en.B: But suppose he has a son who is violent, who sheds blood and does any of these things,
en.R: But suppose this man has a son who is violent and kills people. He does these evil things,

pt.L: Mas, [se] ele gerar um filho violento, derramador de sangue, que fizer qualquer uma destas [coisas],
pt.B: Mas imaginem que ele tenha um filho violento, que derrama sangue e faz qualquer uma dessas coisas,
pt.R: Mas imaginem que esse homem tenha um filho violento, que mata pessoas. Ele faz essas coisas más,

decisions.choice: does any one of these: the son does the evil deeds that the father avoided
alternatives: does to a brother any of these
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is awkward. It may mean "any one of these things", or, with a small change, "to a brother any of these things". Either way the son does the wrongs listed in verses 11-13.

source.text: וְה֕וּא אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה לֹ֣א עָשָׂ֑ה כִּ֣י גַ֤ם אֶל־הֶֽהָרִים֙ אָכַ֔ל וְאֶת־אֵ֥שֶׁת רֵעֵ֖הוּ טִמֵּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: and he himself all these did not do, but also on the mountains he has eaten, and his neighbor's wife he has defiled,

en.L: though he himself did none of these [things], who even eats on the mountains and defiles his neighbor's wife,
en.B: though the father himself did none of them. This son eats at the mountain shrines, defiles his neighbor's wife,
en.R: though his father did none of them. The son eats at the mountain shrines. He commits adultery with his neighbor's wife.

pt.L: embora ele mesmo não tenha feito nenhuma destas [coisas], que até come sobre os montes e contamina a mulher do seu próximo,
pt.B: embora o pai não tenha feito nenhuma delas. Esse filho come nos santuários dos montes, contamina a mulher do seu próximo,
pt.R: embora o pai dele não tenha feito nenhuma delas. O filho come nos santuários dos montes. Comete adultério com a mulher do seu vizinho.

decisions.choice: he himself did none of these: the father did none of these evil things
alternatives: the son did none of the good things
decisions.reason: The words are short. They can mean that the father did none of these evil things, or that the son did none of the good things the father did. Either way the contrast is between the two.

decisions.choice: the father (B); his father (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the father, following the first reading (m1), and name "this son" as the one who does the evil.

source.text: עָנִ֤י וְאֶבְיוֹן֙ הוֹנָ֔ה גְּזֵל֣וֹת גָּזָ֔ל חֲבֹ֖ל לֹ֣א יָשִׁ֑יב וְאֶל־הַגִּלּוּלִים֙ נָשָׂ֣א עֵינָ֔יו תּוֹעֵבָ֖ה עָשָֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: [the] poor and needy he has oppressed, robberies he has committed, a pledge he does not return, and to the idols he has lifted his eyes, abomination he has done,

en.L: has oppressed the poor and needy, has committed robbery, has not returned a pledge, has lifted his eyes to the filthy idols, has done abomination,
en.B: oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return what was pledged, looks to the idols, does detestable things,
en.R: He takes advantage of poor and needy people. He robs people. He does not give back what was given him as a promise to pay. He looks to idols for help, and he does disgusting things.

pt.L: oprime o pobre e o necessitado, comete roubos, não devolve o penhor, levanta os seus olhos para os ídolos imundos, pratica abominação,
pt.B: oprime o pobre e o necessitado, comete roubos, não devolve o que recebeu como penhor, olha para os ídolos, pratica coisas detestáveis,
pt.R: Ele se aproveita dos pobres e dos necessitados. Rouba as pessoas. Não devolve o que recebeu como garantia de pagamento. Olha para os ídolos pedindo ajuda e faz coisas repugnantes.

decisions.choice: filthy idols, abomination (L); idols, detestable things (B); idols, disgusting things (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *gillulim* and *to'evah*.

source.text: בַּנֶּ֧שֶׁךְ נָתַ֛ן וְתַרְבִּ֥ית לָקַ֖ח וָחָ֑י לֹ֣א יִֽחְיֶ֗ה אֵ֣ת כָּל־הַתּוֹעֵב֤וֹת הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ עָשָׂ֔ה מ֣וֹת יוּמָ֔ת דָּמָ֖יו בּ֥וֹ יִהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: at interest he has lent and profit he has taken — will he live? He will not live! All these abominations he has done; he will surely be put to death; his blood will be on him.

en.L: has lent at interest and taken profit; will he then live? He will not live! He has done all these abominations; he will surely be put to death; his blood will be on him.
en.B: and lends at interest and takes profit. Will such a man live? He will not live! He has done all these detestable things; he will surely be put to death. His blood will be on his own head.
en.R: He charges interest when he lends money, and he makes a profit from it. Will a man like that live? No, he will not! He has done all these disgusting things, so he must die. It will be his own fault.

pt.L: empresta com juros e toma lucro; viverá ele? Não viverá! Ele fez todas estas abominações; certamente será morto; o seu sangue estará sobre ele.
pt.B: e empresta com juros e tira lucro. Será que um homem assim vai viver? Não viverá! Ele fez todas essas coisas detestáveis; certamente será morto. O seu sangue cairá sobre a sua própria cabeça.
pt.R: Ele cobra juros quando empresta dinheiro e tira lucro disso. Será que um homem assim vai viver? Não vai! Ele fez todas essas coisas repugnantes, e por isso tem de morrer. A culpa vai ser dele mesmo.

decisions.choice: his blood will be on him: he is responsible for his own death
decisions.reason: The phrase is used in the Law for a person who deserves death; no one else bears the guilt for it (Leviticus 20:9-13).

decisions.choice: he will surely be put to death: the formula of the Law for a capital crime
decisions.reason: The words are those of the death penalty in the Law (Exodus 21:12-17). Here they announce the LORD's judgment.

decisions.choice: It will be his own fault
alternatives: his blood will be on him
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the idiom (m1).

source.text: וְהִנֵּה֙ הוֹלִ֣יד בֵּ֔ן וַיַּ֕רְא אֶת־כָּל־חַטֹּ֥את אָבִ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה וַיִּרְאֶ֕ה וְלֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה כָּהֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And look, he fathers a son, and he sees all the sins of his father that he did, and he sees and does not do like them,

en.L: But look, [if] he fathers a son who sees all the sins that his father did, and he sees and does not do likewise,
en.B: But suppose this man in turn has a son, and the son sees all the sins his father has committed, and though he sees them, he does not do the same,
en.R: But suppose this man has a son. The son sees all the sins his father has committed. He thinks about them, but he does not do the same things.

pt.L: Mas eis que, [se] ele gerar um filho que vê todos os pecados que o seu pai fez, e vê, e não faz coisas semelhantes,
pt.B: Mas imaginem que esse homem, por sua vez, tenha um filho, e o filho veja todos os pecados que o pai cometeu e, mesmo vendo-os, não faça o mesmo,
pt.R: Mas imaginem que esse homem tenha um filho. O filho vê todos os pecados que o pai cometeu. Ele pensa neles, mas não faz as mesmas coisas.

decisions.choice: he sees: he considers and takes warning
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "he sees". With different vowels the second could be read "he fears", and some ancient translations seem to have read it that way. The repetition stresses that he looks hard at his father's life and chooses another way.

decisions.choice: He thinks about them
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the second "sees" (m1).

source.text: עַל־הֶֽהָרִים֙ לֹ֣א אָכָ֔ל וְעֵינָיו֙ לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֔א אֶל־גִּלּוּלֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶת־אֵ֥שֶׁת רֵעֵ֖הוּ לֹ֥א טִמֵּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: on the mountains he has not eaten, and his eyes he has not lifted to the idols of the house of Israel, his neighbor's wife he has not defiled,

en.L: he has not eaten on the mountains, nor lifted his eyes to the filthy idols of the house of Israel, nor defiled his neighbor's wife,
en.B: who does not eat at the mountain shrines or look to the idols of the house of Israel, who does not defile his neighbor's wife,
en.R: He does not eat at the mountain shrines or look to the idols of the people of Israel for help. He does not commit adultery with his neighbor's wife.

pt.L: não come sobre os montes, nem levanta os seus olhos para os ídolos imundos da casa de Israel, nem contamina a mulher do seu próximo,
pt.B: que não come nos santuários dos montes nem olha para os ídolos da casa de Israel, que não contamina a mulher do seu próximo,
pt.R: Ele não come nos santuários dos montes nem olha para os ídolos do povo de Israel pedindo ajuda. Não comete adultério com a mulher do seu vizinho.

decisions.choice: the same list as verse 6
decisions.reason: The grandson keeps the same laws as his grandfather (verse 6). The law about a woman's monthly period is not repeated here.

source.text: וְאִישׁ֙ לֹ֣א הוֹנָ֔ה חֲבֹל֙ לֹ֣א חָבָ֔ל וּגְזֵלָ֖ה לֹ֣א גָזָ֑ל לַחְמוֹ֙ לְרָעֵ֣ב נָתָ֔ן וְעֵר֖וֹם כִּסָּה־בָֽגֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: and no one he has oppressed, a pledge he has not taken, and robbery he has not committed; his bread to the hungry he has given, and the naked he has covered with clothing,

en.L: has not oppressed anyone, has not taken a pledge, has committed no robbery, has given his bread to the hungry and covered the naked with clothing,
en.B: who does not oppress anyone or demand a pledge, who does not rob but gives his food to the hungry and clothes the naked,
en.R: He does not take advantage of anyone or demand something as a promise to pay back a loan. He does not rob anyone. He gives food to hungry people and clothes to people who have nothing to wear.

pt.L: não oprime ninguém, não toma penhor, não comete roubo, dá o seu pão ao faminto e cobre de roupa o nu,
pt.B: que não oprime ninguém nem exige penhor, que não rouba, mas dá o seu alimento ao faminto e veste o nu,
pt.R: Ele não se aproveita de ninguém nem exige uma garantia de pagamento por um empréstimo. Não rouba ninguém. Dá comida a quem tem fome e roupa a quem não tem o que vestir.

decisions.choice: has not taken a pledge: he goes beyond returning it
decisions.reason: In verse 7 the righteous man returns a pledge; here the grandson does not even take one.

source.text: מֵעָנִ֞י הֵשִׁ֣יב יָד֗וֹ נֶ֤שֶׁךְ וְתַרְבִּית֙ לֹ֣א לָקָ֔ח מִשְׁפָּטַ֣י עָשָׂ֔ה בְּחֻקּוֹתַ֖י הָלָ֑ךְ ה֗וּא לֹ֥א יָמ֛וּת בַּעֲוֺ֥ן אָבִ֖יו חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: from the poor he has turned back his hand, interest and profit he has not taken; my judgments he has done, in my statutes he has walked — he will not die for the iniquity of his father; he will surely live.

en.L: has turned back his hand from the poor, has not taken interest or profit, has done {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments [and] walked in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, he will not die for the iniquity of his father; he will surely live.
en.B: who keeps his hand from harming the poor and takes no interest or profit, who obeys {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings and follows {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes. He will not die for his father's guilt; he will surely live.
en.R: He does not harm poor people. He does not charge interest or make a profit from loans. He obeys {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rules and lives by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws. That man will not die because of his father's sins. He will certainly live.

pt.L: desvia a sua mão do pobre, não toma juros nem lucro, pratica os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} juízos [e] anda nos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos, ele não morrerá pela iniquidade do seu pai; certamente viverá.
pt.B: que não levanta a mão contra o pobre e não cobra juros nem tira lucro, que obedece às {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} ordenanças e segue os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos. Ele não morrerá pela culpa do pai; certamente viverá.
pt.R: Ele não faz mal aos pobres. Não cobra juros nem tira lucro dos empréstimos. Obedece às {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} regras e vive pelas {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} leis. Esse homem não vai morrer por causa dos pecados do pai. Ele com certeza vai viver.

decisions.choice: from the poor
decisions.reason: The Septuagint reads "from injustice", as in verse 8. The Hebrew "from the poor" means that he keeps his hand from harming them.

decisions.choice: he will not die for the iniquity of his father: the answer to the proverb
decisions.reason: Here the principle of verse 4 is applied to the grandson: his father's sins do not condemn him.

decisions.choice: iniquity (L); guilt (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *'awon*.

source.text: אָבִ֞יו כִּֽי־עָ֣שַׁק עֹ֗שֶׁק גָּזַל֙ גֵּ֣זֶל אָ֔ח וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ט֛וֹב עָשָׂ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ עַמָּ֑יו וְהִנֵּה־מֵ֖ת בַּעֲוֺנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: His father, because he practiced extortion, robbed [his] brother of robbery, and what is not good he did among his people — look, he will die for his iniquity.

en.L: As for his father, because he practiced extortion, committed robbery against a brother, and did what is not good among his people, look, he will die for his iniquity.
en.B: But as for his father, he will die for his own guilt, because he extorted from others, robbed his brother and did what was not good among his people.
en.R: But his father will die for his own sins, because he cheated people, robbed his brother and did evil among his people.

pt.L: Quanto ao seu pai, porque praticou extorsão, cometeu roubo contra um irmão e fez o que não é bom no meio do seu povo, eis que ele morrerá pela sua iniquidade.
pt.B: Mas, quanto ao pai, ele morrerá pela sua própria culpa, porque extorquiu os outros, roubou o seu irmão e fez o que não era bom no meio do seu povo.
pt.R: Mas o pai vai morrer pelos seus próprios pecados, porque enganou as pessoas, roubou o seu irmão e fez o mal no meio do seu povo.

decisions.choice: a brother: a fellow Israelite
decisions.reason: "Brother" here can mean a member of the same people, not only of the same family (Leviticus 25:35-36).

source.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם מַדֻּ֛עַ לֹא־נָשָׂ֥א הַבֵּ֖ן בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֑ב וְהַבֵּ֞ן מִשְׁפָּ֧ט וּצְדָקָ֣ה עָשָׂ֗ה אֵ֣ת כָּל־חֻקּוֹתַ֥י שָׁמַ֛ר וַיַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָ֖ם חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you say, Why does the son not bear the iniquity of the father? The son has done justice and righteousness, all my statutes he has kept and done them; he will surely live.

en.L: Yet you say, "Why does the son not bear the iniquity of the father?" The son has done justice and righteousness; he has kept all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and done them; he will surely live.
en.B: Yet you ask, "Why should the son not share the guilt of his father?" The son has done what is just and right and has been careful to keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes, so he will surely live.
en.R: But you ask, "Why should the son not be punished for his father's sins?" The son has done what is fair and right. He has carefully obeyed all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws, so he will certainly live.

pt.L: Mas vocês dizem: "Por que o filho não leva a iniquidade do pai?" O filho praticou o direito e a justiça; guardou todos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos e os cumpriu; certamente viverá.
pt.B: Mas vocês perguntam: "Por que o filho não deve partilhar a culpa do pai?" O filho fez o que é justo e certo e teve o cuidado de guardar todos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos; por isso certamente viverá.
pt.R: Mas vocês perguntam: "Por que o filho não deve ser castigado pelos pecados do pai?" O filho fez o que é correto e certo. Obedeceu com cuidado a todas as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} leis, e por isso vai viver com certeza.

decisions.choice: why does the son not bear the iniquity of the father: the hearers' objection
decisions.reason: The exiles expected sons to share their fathers' punishment, as the proverb of verse 2 assumes. The LORD answers with the case he has just described.

decisions.choice: bear the iniquity: carry the guilt and its punishment
decisions.reason: To bear someone's iniquity is to suffer the punishment due for it (Leviticus 5:1; Numbers 14:33-34).

source.text: הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא־יִשָּׂ֣א׀בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב וְאָב֙ לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הַבֵּ֔ן צִדְקַ֤ת הַצַּדִּיק֙ עָלָ֣יו תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה וְרִשְׁעַ֥ת הָרָשָׁ֖ע עָלָ֥יו תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The soul who sins, it will die. A son will not bear the iniquity of the father, and a father will not bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous on him will be, and the wickedness of the wicked on him will be.

en.L: The soul who sins, it will die. A son will not bear the iniquity of the father, and a father will not bear the iniquity of the son. The righteousness of the righteous will be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked will be upon him.
en.B: The person who sins is the one who will die. A {{gender:child|son}} will not share the guilt of a {{gender:parent|father}}, and a {{gender:parent|father}} will not share the guilt of a {{gender:child|son}}. The righteousness of the righteous will be their own, and the wickedness of the wicked will be their own.
en.R: The person who sins is the one who will die. {{gender:Children|Sons}} will not be punished for their {{gender:parents'|fathers'}} sins, and {{gender:parents|fathers}} will not be punished for their {{gender:children's|sons'}} sins. Good people will be rewarded for the good they do, and evil people will be punished for the evil they do.

pt.L: A alma que peca, ela é que morrerá. O filho não levará a iniquidade do pai, e o pai não levará a iniquidade do filho. A justiça do justo estará sobre ele, e a impiedade do ímpio estará sobre ele.
pt.B: Quem morrerá é a pessoa que pecar. Os filhos não partilharão a culpa dos pais, e os pais não partilharão a culpa dos filhos. A justiça do justo será dele, e a maldade do ímpio será dele.
pt.R: Quem vai morrer é a pessoa que pecar. Os filhos não vão ser castigados pelos pecados dos pais, e os pais não vão ser castigados pelos pecados dos filhos. As pessoas boas vão receber a recompensa pelo bem que fazem, e as pessoas más vão receber o castigo pelo mal que fazem.

decisions.choice: a son will not bear the iniquity of the father: the law of Deuteronomy 24:16
decisions.reason: The Law says that parents shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their parents; each is to die for their own sin (Deuteronomy 24:16; compare 2 Kings 14:6).

decisions.choice: the soul: the person, as in verse 4
decisions.reason: See verse 4.

decisions.choice: the soul (L); the person (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *nefesh* here, as in verse 4.

decisions.choice: child, parent (B); children, parents (R), with son and father as the alternatives
decisions.reason: Here the principle covers every parent and child, so the gender setting is used, as in verse 4.

decisions.choice: will be rewarded for the good they do ... will be punished for the evil they do
decisions.reason: "Will be on him" means that each person receives what their own conduct deserves. Readable says so plainly.

decisions.choice: os filhos ... os pais, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: As in verse 4: the plural "os filhos", "os pais" already takes in daughters and mothers, so the English gender spans have no counterpart.

source.text: וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ מִכָּל־חַטֹּאתָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְשָׁמַר֙ אֶת־כָּל־חֻקּוֹתַ֔י וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָ֑ה חָיֹ֥ה יִחְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the wicked, if he turns from all his sins that he has done, and keeps all my statutes and does justice and righteousness, he will surely live; he will not die.

en.L: But the wicked [person], if he turns from all his sins that he has done and keeps all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and does justice and righteousness, he will surely live; he will not die.
en.B: But if wicked people turn away from all the sins they have committed, keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and do what is just and right, they will surely live; they will not die.
en.R: But suppose evil people stop doing all the sins they have been doing. They obey all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and do what is fair and right. Then they will certainly live. They will not die.

pt.L: Mas o ímpio, se ele se desviar de todos os pecados que cometeu e guardar todos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos e praticar o direito e a justiça, certamente viverá; não morrerá.
pt.B: Mas, se os ímpios se desviarem de todos os pecados que cometeram, guardarem todos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} estatutos e fizerem o que é justo e certo, certamente viverão; não morrerão.
pt.R: Mas imaginem que as pessoas más deixem de cometer todos os pecados que vinham cometendo. Elas obedecem a todas as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} leis e fazem o que é correto e certo. Então elas vão viver com certeza. Não vão morrer.

decisions.choice: if the wicked turns: a person's past does not seal their fate
decisions.reason: The chapter now turns from the generations to a single life. As a son is not condemned for his father, so a person is not held to their own past if they turn from it.

decisions.choice: wicked people ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "he" for any person. Balanced and Readable use "people" and "they", which include everyone, as the Hebrew means. Literal keeps the singular "he" of the Hebrew.

source.text: כָּל־פְּשָׁעָיו֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה לֹ֥א יִזָּכְר֖וּ ל֑וֹ בְּצִדְקָת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה יִֽחְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: All his transgressions that he has done will not be remembered against him; for his righteousness that he has done he will live.

en.L: All his transgressions that he has committed will not be remembered against him; because of his righteousness that he has done, he will live.
en.B: None of the rebellious acts they have committed will be remembered against them. Because of the righteousness they have practiced, they will live.
en.R: None of the sins they have committed will be held against them. They will live because they have done what is right.

pt.L: Nenhuma das suas transgressões que cometeu será lembrada contra ele; pela justiça que praticou, viverá.
pt.B: Nenhuma das rebeldias que cometeram será lembrada contra eles. Por causa da justiça que praticaram, viverão.
pt.R: Nenhum dos pecados que elas cometeram vai ser lembrado contra elas. Elas vão viver porque fizeram o que é certo.

decisions.choice: will not be remembered: will not be held against him
decisions.reason: For God to "remember" sins is to act on them in judgment (Hosea 8:13). Their past is no longer counted (compare Isaiah 43:25).

decisions.choice: transgressions (L); rebellious acts (B); sins (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *pesha'*.

source.text: הֶחָפֹ֤ץ אֶחְפֹּץ֙ מ֣וֹת רָשָׁ֔ע נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֲל֛וֹא בְּשׁוּב֥וֹ מִדְּרָכָ֖יו וְחָיָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Do I really take pleasure in [the] death of [the] wicked, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, [and] not in his turning from his ways so that he lives?

en.L: Do I indeed take pleasure in the death of the wicked, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, and not in his turning from his ways so that he may live?
en.B: Is it any pleasure to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when the wicked die? declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. Would I not rather that they turn from their ways and live?
en.R: Do you think I am happy when evil people die? says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. No! I want them to turn away from their evil ways and live.

pt.L: Tenho eu de fato prazer na morte do ímpio, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, e não em que ele se desvie dos seus caminhos e viva?
pt.B: Será que a morte dos ímpios {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dá algum prazer? declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Não prefiro que eles deixem os seus caminhos e vivam?
pt.R: Vocês acham que eu fico feliz quando as pessoas más morrem? diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Não! Eu quero que elas deixem os seus maus caminhos e vivam.

decisions.choice: the LORD takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked: he wants them to turn and live
decisions.reason: This is the heart of the chapter, repeated in verse 32 and 33:11. The LORD's judgment is real, but his desire is for the wicked to turn. Compare 1 Timothy 2:4 and 2 Peter 3:9.

source.text: וּבְשׁ֨וּב צַדִּ֤יק מִצִּדְקָתוֹ֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֔וֶל כְּכֹ֨ל הַתּוֹעֵב֜וֹת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֧ה הָרָשָׁ֛ע יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה וָחָ֑י כָּל־צִדְקֹתָ֤יו אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂה֙ לֹ֣א תִזָּכַ֔רְנָה בְּמַעֲל֧וֹ אֲשֶׁר־מָעַ֛ל וּבְחַטָּאת֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־חָטָ֖א בָּ֥ם יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And when the righteous turns from his righteousness and does injustice, according to all the abominations that the wicked does he does — will he live? All his righteous deeds that he has done will not be remembered; for his unfaithfulness that he has committed and for his sin that he has sinned, for them he will die.

en.L: But when a righteous [person] turns away from his righteousness and does injustice, according to all the abominations that the wicked [person] does, will he live? All his righteous deeds that he has done will not be remembered; for his unfaithfulness that he has committed and for his sin that he has sinned, for them he will die.
en.B: But if righteous people turn away from their righteousness and do wrong, committing all the same detestable things that the wicked do, will they live? None of the righteous things they have done will be remembered. Because of the unfaithfulness they are guilty of and the sins they have committed, they will die.
en.R: But suppose good people stop doing what is right and start doing wrong. They do the same disgusting things that evil people do. Will they live? No! None of the good things they did will be remembered. They will die because they were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and committed sins.

pt.L: Mas, quando o justo se desviar da sua justiça e praticar a injustiça, segundo todas as abominações que o ímpio pratica, viverá ele? Nenhuma das obras justas que praticou será lembrada; pela infidelidade que cometeu e pelo pecado que pecou, por eles morrerá.
pt.B: Mas, se os justos se desviarem da sua justiça e praticarem o mal, cometendo as mesmas coisas detestáveis que os ímpios cometem, será que viverão? Nenhuma das coisas justas que fizeram será lembrada. Por causa da infidelidade de que são culpados e dos pecados que cometeram, eles morrerão.
pt.R: Mas imaginem que as pessoas boas deixem de fazer o que é certo e comecem a fazer o mal. Elas fazem as mesmas coisas repugnantes que as pessoas más fazem. Será que vão viver? Não! Nenhuma das coisas boas que fizeram vai ser lembrada. Elas vão morrer porque foram infiéis a {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e cometeram pecados.

decisions.choice: if the righteous turns away: past goodness is no protection
decisions.reason: The principle works both ways. A person who turns from righteousness to wickedness cannot rely on their past (compare 3:20). The chapter speaks of a person's settled direction, not of single faults.

decisions.choice: unfaithfulness: breach of trust against God
decisions.reason: As in 17:20, *ma'al* is a betrayal of what was owed to God.

source.text: וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י שִׁמְעוּ־נָא֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֲדַרְכִּי֙ לֹ֣א יִתָּכֵ֔ן הֲלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you say, Not right is the way of [the] Lord. Hear now, house of Israel: Is my way not right? Is it not your ways [that] are not right?

en.L: Yet you say, "Not right is the way of the Lord." Hear now, house of Israel: Is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} way not right? Is it not your ways that are not right?
en.B: Yet you say, "The Lord's way is not fair." Listen, house of Israel: Is it {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} way that is not fair? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
en.R: But you say, "What the Lord does is not fair." Listen, people of Israel. Is what I do unfair? No, it is what you do that is unfair!

pt.L: Mas vocês dizem: "Não é reto o caminho do Senhor." Ouçam agora, casa de Israel: Não é reto o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} caminho? Não são os caminhos de vocês que não são retos?
pt.B: Mas vocês dizem: "O caminho do Senhor não é justo." Ouçam, casa de Israel: É o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} caminho que não é justo? Não são os caminhos de vocês que são injustos?
pt.R: Mas vocês dizem: "O que o Senhor faz não é justo." Escutem, povo de Israel. O que eu faço é injusto? Não, o que vocês fazem é que é injusto!

decisions.choice: not right: not fair, not measured by a just standard
decisions.reason: The verb means to be weighed or measured. The people say that the LORD's dealings do not measure up; the LORD answers that their own do not.

decisions.choice: What the Lord does
decisions.reason: Readable says what "way" means here: the LORD's dealings. "Lord" here translates *Adonai*.

decisions.choice: reto (L); justo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to be weighed or measured (m1). Literal says "reto", what measures true; Balanced and Readable say "justo", fair, as the English says "fair".

source.text: בְּשׁוּב־צַדִּ֧יק מִצִּדְקָת֛וֹ וְעָ֥שָׂה עָ֖וֶל וּמֵ֣ת עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם בְּעַוְל֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה יָמֽוּת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: When the righteous turns from his righteousness and does injustice and dies for them, for his injustice that he has done he will die.

en.L: When a righteous [person] turns away from his righteousness and does injustice, and dies for them, for his injustice that he has done he will die.
en.B: If righteous people turn away from their righteousness and do wrong, they will die for it; because of the wrong they have done, they will die.
en.R: If good people stop doing what is right and start doing wrong, they will die. They will die because of the wrong things they have done.

pt.L: Quando o justo se desviar da sua justiça e praticar a injustiça, e morrer por elas, pela injustiça que praticou morrerá.
pt.B: Se os justos se desviarem da sua justiça e praticarem o mal, morrerão por isso; por causa do mal que fizeram, morrerão.
pt.R: Se as pessoas boas deixarem de fazer o que é certo e começarem a fazer o mal, elas vão morrer. Vão morrer por causa das coisas erradas que fizeram.

decisions.choice: and dies for them: dies because of these wrongs
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to the wrongs he has done. The verse restates verse 24 as the LORD's answer to the charge of verse 25.

source.text: וּבְשׁ֣וּב רָשָׁ֗ע מֵֽרִשְׁעָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָ֑ה ה֖וּא אֶת־נַפְשׁ֥וֹ יְחַיֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And when the wicked turns from his wickedness that he has done, and does justice and righteousness, he will keep his soul alive.

en.L: And when a wicked [person] turns away from his wickedness that he has done and does justice and righteousness, he will keep his soul alive.
en.B: And if wicked people turn away from the wickedness they have committed and do what is just and right, they will save their lives.
en.R: And if evil people stop doing evil and start doing what is fair and right, they will save their lives.

pt.L: E, quando o ímpio se desviar da impiedade que praticou e praticar o direito e a justiça, ele conservará viva a sua alma.
pt.B: E, se os ímpios se desviarem da maldade que cometeram e fizerem o que é justo e certo, salvarão a sua vida.
pt.R: E, se as pessoas más deixarem de fazer o mal e começarem a fazer o que é correto e certo, elas vão salvar a própria vida.

decisions.choice: his soul: his life
decisions.reason: Here *nefesh* means "life": he will keep himself alive.

source.text: וַיִּרְאֶ֣ה וַיָּ֔שָׁב מִכָּל־פְּשָׁעָ֖יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה חָי֥וֹ יִחְיֶ֖ה לֹ֥א יָמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he considered and turned from all his transgressions that he had done; he will surely live; he will not die.

en.L: Because he considered and turned away from all his transgressions that he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die.
en.B: Because they thought it over and turned away from all the rebellious acts they had committed, they will surely live; they will not die.
en.R: They thought about what they were doing, and they stopped sinning. So they will certainly live. They will not die.

pt.L: Porque considerou e se desviou de todas as transgressões que tinha cometido, certamente viverá; não morrerá.
pt.B: Porque refletiram e se desviaram de todas as rebeldias que tinham cometido, certamente viverão; não morrerão.
pt.R: Elas pensaram no que estavam fazendo e pararam de pecar. Por isso vão viver com certeza. Não vão morrer.

decisions.choice: he considered: he saw what he was doing and took it to heart
decisions.reason: The verb "see" here means to look at one's life and recognize the truth about it, as the grandson did in verse 14.

source.text: וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י הַדְּרָכַ֞י לֹ֤א יִתָּֽכְנּוּ֙בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֲלֹ֥א דַרְכֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And says the house of Israel, Not right is the way of [the] Lord. My ways, are they not right, house of Israel? Is it not your ways [that] are not right?

en.L: But the house of Israel says, "Not right is the way of the Lord." Are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways not right, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are not right?
en.B: Yet the house of Israel says, "The Lord's way is not fair." Are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ways unfair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
en.R: But the people of Israel say, "What the Lord does is not fair." People of Israel, is what I do unfair? No, it is what you do that is unfair!

pt.L: Mas a casa de Israel diz: "Não é reto o caminho do Senhor." Não são retos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} caminhos, casa de Israel? Não são os caminhos de vocês que não são retos?
pt.B: Mas a casa de Israel diz: "O caminho do Senhor não é justo." São injustos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} caminhos, casa de Israel? Não são os caminhos de vocês que são injustos?
pt.R: Mas o povo de Israel diz: "O que o Senhor faz não é justo." Povo de Israel, o que eu faço é injusto? Não, o que vocês fazem é que é injusto!

decisions.choice: the same charge and answer as verse 25
decisions.reason: The repetition frames the chapter's last appeal (verses 30-32).

source.text: לָכֵן֩ אִ֨ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֜יו אֶשְׁפֹּ֤ט אֶתְכֶם֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה שׁ֤וּבוּ וְהָשִׁ֨יבוּ֙ מִכָּל־פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם לְמִכְשׁ֖וֹל עָוֺֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore each according to his ways I will judge you, house of Israel, declares [the] Lord Yahweh. Turn and turn away from all your transgressions, so that it will not become to you a stumbling block of iniquity.

en.L: Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. Turn, and turn away from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be a stumbling block for you.
en.B: Therefore, house of Israel, I will judge each of you according to your ways, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. Repent and turn away from all your rebellious acts, so that your guilt will not bring you down.
en.R: So, people of Israel, I will judge each of you by what you have done, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. Turn back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! Turn away from all your sins, so that your sin will not destroy you.

pt.L: Por isso eu julgarei vocês, casa de Israel, cada um segundo os seus caminhos, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Voltem e desviem-se de todas as suas transgressões, para que a iniquidade não seja para vocês um tropeço.
pt.B: Por isso, casa de Israel, julgarei cada um de vocês segundo os seus caminhos, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Arrependam-se e afastem-se de todas as suas rebeldias, para que a culpa não os derrube.
pt.R: Por isso, povo de Israel, vou julgar cada um de vocês pelo que fez, diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Voltem para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}! Abandonem todos os seus pecados, para que o pecado não destrua vocês.

decisions.choice: turn and turn away: repent, change direction
decisions.reason: The verb *shuv* means to turn around. The second form means to turn oneself (or others) away from sin. Together they call for a full change of life.

decisions.choice: a stumbling block of iniquity: something that makes them fall into guilt and judgment
decisions.reason: Ezekiel uses the phrase for what causes Israel to fall (7:19; 14:3-4).

decisions.choice: Turn back to me
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that turning means coming back to the LORD, which the call implies.

source.text: הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ מֵעֲלֵיכֶ֗ם אֶת־כָּל־פִּשְׁעֵיכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֣ם בָּ֔ם וַעֲשׂ֥וּ לָכֶ֛ם לֵ֥ב חָדָ֖שׁ וְר֣וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וְלָ֥מָּה תָמֻ֖תוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Cast away from you all your transgressions which you have transgressed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; and why will you die, house of Israel?

en.L: Cast away from you all your transgressions by which you have transgressed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit; and why will you die, house of Israel?
en.B: Throw away all the rebellious acts you have committed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why would you die, house of Israel?
en.R: Get rid of all the sins you have committed. Get a new heart and a new spirit. People of Israel, why should you die?

pt.L: Lancem de vocês todas as transgressões com que transgrediram, e façam para vocês um coração novo e um espírito novo; pois por que morrerão, casa de Israel?
pt.B: Joguem fora todas as rebeldias que vocês cometeram e façam para si um coração novo e um espírito novo. Por que vocês morreriam, casa de Israel?
pt.R: Livrem-se de todos os pecados que vocês cometeram. Tenham um coração novo e um espírito novo. Povo de Israel, por que vocês haveriam de morrer?

decisions.choice: make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit: a command that the LORD elsewhere promises to fulfill
decisions.reason: Here the people are told to make a new heart and spirit; in 11:19 and 36:26 the LORD promises to give them. The call and the promise belong together: the LORD commands what he himself makes possible.

decisions.choice: spirit: the inner life, the will and attitude
decisions.reason: *Ruach* here is the human spirit, not the Spirit of God that enters Ezekiel (see the note at 2:2), so it is lowercase.

decisions.choice: have transgressed (L); have committed (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb *pasha'* follows the settled wording ("transgress" / "rebel" / "sin"), with the object already naming the sins.

decisions.choice: um coração novo e um espírito novo
decisions.reason: The pair of 11:19 and 36:26 (m1), with "espírito" lowercase for the human spirit (m2), and the adjective after the noun, as Portuguese says it plainly. Kept the same at every level so that 36:26 can echo it.

source.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הַמֵּ֔ת נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: For not I take pleasure in [the] death of the one dying, declares [the] Lord Yahweh. So turn and live!

en.L: For I take no pleasure in the death of the one who dies, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. So turn, and live!
en.B: The death of anyone gives {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no pleasure, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. So turn back and live!
en.R: I do not want anyone to die, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. So turn back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and live!

pt.L: Pois não tenho prazer na morte de quem morre, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Portanto, voltem e vivam!
pt.B: Não {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dá prazer a morte de ninguém, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Portanto, voltem-se e vivam!
pt.R: Eu não quero que ninguém morra, diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Por isso, voltem para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} e vivam!

decisions.choice: I take no pleasure in the death of anyone: verse 23 again
decisions.reason: The chapter ends as verse 23 does, with the LORD's desire that people live, and an invitation.
